attributes.residual: THE LEVER IS INSUFFICIENT ON THIS FUNCTION, and the evidence is specific enough to bound the law. Target's preheader is `lfd f30,@lbl_80348370` then `lfd f31,@lbl_803483B0`; poolval gives lbl_80348370 = 0x4330000080000000 (the s32->f64 bias) and lbl_803483B0 = 0.00390625, so target puts the BIAS in the low callee-saved FPR and the divisor above it. BEFORE the edit ours was `lfd f30,@lbl_803483B0` / `lfd f31,@@193` -- the scaffold local in f30, exactly the run-40 symptom. AFTER the edit ours is `lfd f30,@@222` / `lfd f31,@@193`, and pooldump --ours identifies @193 as the bias at .sdata2+0x0 and @222 as 0.00390625 at .sdata2+0x8. So both constants became anonymous as intended, our pool order (bias first, then the divisor) already MATCHES the target's address order -- and the deal order did NOT change: the divisor still takes f30 and the bias still f31. Deleting the named local is therefore NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT for the deal order; something else pins it here, most plausibly the surrounding addressing form, since the function's dominant residual is three target-only `add` instructions (target keeps loop base pointers in registers with `add r17,r6,r8` / `add r20,r6,r7` while we recompute with `addi r17,r4,128`), and that register pressure is what the FPR deal is scheduled around. NEXT LANE ON show_gold: close the addressing form first and re-probe the literalisation afterwards -- probes in this project are alignment-sensitive and this one is a candidate to flip once the three adds land.
